# requireRelative

<link-summary>Returns the value as a relative path, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireRelative() — Returns the value as a relative path, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireRelative(path: unknown, message: string = "Expected a relative path."): string;
```

The exact complement of `isAbsolute`: anything that does not start at a root, which includes the empty string.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                              | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`                                                 | `unknown` | The value to validate as a relative path.                     |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a relative path."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a relative path.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                         |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a relative path. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireRelative("docs/readme.md"); // => "docs/readme.md"
requireRelative("./a"); // => "./a"
requireRelative("/var/log"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireRelative("https://example.com/a"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
